title: Puebloans - Aztec Regional System
capsule: As Chaco Canyon's role as a central place ended around 1150, the great houses at Aztec and Salmon on the Animas and San Juan rivers - themselves built a generation earlier as Chacoan outliers - emerged as the successor focus of the Ancestral Puebloan regional network, their multi-storied masonry pueblos and great kivas echoing Chacoan architectural forms. The Aztec Regional System never matched Chaco's earlier scale of ceremonial centralization, and by around 1300 the entire Four Corners region, including the Aztec and Mesa Verde communities, was depopulated in a coordinated southward migration whose descendants became the Pueblo peoples of the Rio Grande and Hopi mesas.
